summary.oneLiner: Narmada Gelatines Limited is a single-segment manufacturer of gelatine and related products (ossein, di-calcium phosphate) serving pharmaceutical, food and nutraceutical customers, with gelatine contributing 70.77% of turnover in FY2025-26.
summary.business: The Company is engaged in only one segment, namely the manufacture and sale of gelatine and related products like ossein and di-calcium phosphate (DCP), and accordingly reports no separate segments under Ind AS-108. Gelatine accounted for 70.77% of turnover and DCP 29.15% during the year under review. Its gelatine goes into applications the Company describes across food and beverage, pharmaceuticals (hard and soft capsules, tablet coating, syrups), cosmetics, photography and nutraceuticals.

related.name: India Gelatine and Chemicals Limited (IGCL)
related.note: Narmada Gelatines acquired a 14.14% equity stake during FY2024-25. Although the direct holding is below the Section 2(6) threshold, IGCL is treated as an associate because the Company together with its promoters collectively holds more than 20% of IGCL's equity share capital and thereby exercises significant influence. IGCL became an associate with effect from 05 December 2024, and the salient features of its financial statements are given in Form AOC-1 at Annexure-V. Same industry - gelatine and chemicals.

currentContext.expansion: The Company's FY2025-26 disclosures describe efficiency and utility capex at its Jabalpur works rather than any gelatine capacity expansion. Under conservation of energy it installed an Ultra-filtration (UF) Plant for gelatine concentration, thereby eliminating use of the old SSP Evaporator to save on steam and electricity, and replaced steam radiators with hot water radiators to reduce steam consumption. For environment conservation it installed rain water harvesting and revamped the CICON Plant to utilise treated water for process, reducing fresh water consumption. On alternate energy, 'The solar plant within the Factory premises commissioned', with capital investment on energy conservation equipment (Solar Plant) stated at Rs 8.89 Crores. On technology absorption, 'Process control for improvement of product quality and the implementation of SAP is currently underway and progressing as planned', with the benefit described as improvement in product mix giving better realization; no technology was imported. R&D was expensed only - recurring R&D expenditure with nil capital R&D. No installed-capacity table, no new plant, line or greenfield project and no commissioning timetable for capacity is disclosed in this bundle.

risks.risk: Substitution by plant-based gelatin alternatives, plus cultural and religious prohibitions on animal-source gelatine
risks.note: Management names this as the primary market barrier: 'The rise of plant-based gelatin substitutes, fueled by rising demand for vegetarian and vegan goods, is one of the primary market barriers. Traditional gelatin made from animal sources is affected due to this trend'. It attacks the core product rather than a segment, so it is structural for a single-product gelatine maker.

risks.risk: Raw material availability and price, including reliance on imports versus domestic supply
risks.note: The cautionary statement lists 'raw material availability, import and exports of raw material and finished goods' among the factors outside the Company's control. The FY26 benefit came from a global gelatine price fall in the second half that cut raw-material cost and let the Company import at competitive prices, easing 'pressure in domestic raw material supplies' - the same mechanism reverses if global prices rise.

'The Company is engaged in only one segment, namely, manufacture and sale of gelatine and related products like assein and di-calcium phosphate (DCP) and as such there are no reportable segments as per Ind AS-108.' With gelatine 70.77% and DCP 29.15% of turnover, there is no diversification to absorb a shock to gelatine demand or pricing.

risks.risk: Gelatine realisation deflation - price risk decoupling volume growth from revenue
risks.note: During FY2025-26 gelatine sales volume rose 16.17% but the average selling price of gelatine fell 5.20%; DCP volume rose 11.35% with its average selling price up 17.17%. The gelatine price direction is set by the global market, not by the Company, so volume gains can be offset by realisation.

risks.risk: Energy and fuel cost exposure, principally coal
risks.note: Power and fuel cost fell 4.98% 'due to decrease in the coal prices and consumption', and profit growth was attributed to 'better yield and lower consumption of power and fuel'. A material part of the FY26 margin expansion is therefore a commodity input tailwind that can reverse.

risks.risk: Geopolitical instability affecting global trade flows
risks.note: 'Prolonged geopolitical instability, including the middle-east conflict, may continue to impact global trade flows and overall market sentiments.' This bears on both imported raw material and exports, which grew sharply in FY26.

The cautionary statement lists 'government regulations, changes in taxation' among factors that could make a significant difference to operations and over which the Company has no direct control. The business is also subject to food-safety, pollution-control, legal-metrology and factories legislation per the secretarial audit scope.

risks.risk: Demand and macro conditions plus natural calamities outside management control
risks.note: The forward-looking-statement caveat names 'economic conditions, affecting demand and supply ... natural calamities, on which the Company does not have any direct control' as reasons actual results may differ from stated expectations.
